title: A Bengaluru startup just launched the world's first commercial OptoSAR satellite
sources: Business Standard, May 2026 - GalaxEye launches Mission Drishti, world's first OptoSAR satellite platform
SatNews, May 2026 - GalaxEye successfully launches Mission Drishti OptoSAR satellite
caption:
Optical cameras can't see through clouds. Radar can't see color or texture. One Bengaluru startup just put both on a single satellite - a world first.

GalaxEye's Mission Drishti launched in May 2026, weighing 190 kilograms - India's largest privately built Earth observation satellite. Its sensor suite, called SyncFused, combines electro-optical imaging and synthetic aperture radar on one platform, enabling all-weather, day-and-night imaging neither sensor type can do alone.

A satellite that can only see on a clear day is only half a tool. This is the half that was missing, built by a company that isn't a government space agency.
